outputs.summary: Independent public snapshots and synthetic consumer language point to a time-bounded confidence-under-pressure opportunity; commerce progression is positive but modest.
strongestSupport: Search direction, weather context, and news diffusion come from separate public source families.
Synthetic consumer connects repeat confidence despite sweat across four aggregate city cells.
strongestCounterEvidence: Synthetic category commerce progression is weak and cannot establish incrementality.
National stock and match-footage rights are not ready.

skeptic.alternativeExplanation: Seasonal heat and match attention may explain the movement without a brand-specific demand shift.
skeptic.sensitivityNote: If a later review assumes 70% source concentration, apply a deterministic 14-point penalty (70 × 0.20).

outputs.summary: Persistent search language and synthetic routine narratives support a durable strategic shift, while claim and product readiness remain low.
strongestSupport: The search pattern persists beyond one event window.
Synthetic consumers describe scalp-first routines and ingredient scrutiny.
strongestCounterEvidence: The fixture has no ready product-specific scalp claim.
Synthetic commerce intent is not yet strong enough for activation.

skeptic.alternativeExplanation: Interest may remain informational and fail to convert to a distinct hair-care routine.

outputs.summary: The visible spike is concentrated in one creator family and lacks search or commerce progression.
strongestSupport: One public creator/search snapshot shows attention.
strongestCounterEvidence: Ninety percent of visible attention sits in one creator family.
Synthetic commerce and category-search progression are effectively flat.

skeptic.alternativeExplanation: Paid seeding, creator novelty, or entertainment value explains the spike better than category demand.
